proposals.evidence: Probable regional loan from the Arabic-origin baʿd/bād after family. OPED9343 directly attests Pashto baʿd with alternative bād, after/afterward/then, and labels its origin Arabic. Dameli final d > t is compatible with Perder’s independently described word-final obstruent devoicing (pp43–44). This supports the comparison, but does not distinguish Pashto transmission from other regional routes. The short-a bat citations are grouped with bāt without silently normalizing the source forms. Do not use the homographic bāt speech/talk link under CDIAL11348 vārttā. The bǣt vowel variant and yē ta bāt whole phrase are excluded here.
